name: South Dakota

code.name: South Dakota Codified Laws (SDCL), Title 12 (Elections) and the municipal and school-district election chapters 9-13 and 13-7, as reprinted in the South Dakota Secretary of State's 'Election Code' book
code.edition: Secretary of State - South Dakota, Election Code, 'Last Updated: June 12, 2026' (the book says Title 12 is the statutes in effect on July 1, 2026, and that statutes are subject to change after each legislative session)

sd-code2026.citation: SDCL 12-6-51.1 (runoff, tie for second place), 12-21-8 to 12-21-16 (recounts), 12-21-43 (tie after recount determined by lot), 9-13-27.2 to 9-13-27.4 (municipal ties and recounts), 13-7-19.1 and 13-7-19.2 (school board ties and recounts), as reprinted in the Secretary of State's 2026 Election Code
sd-code2026.note: A documented download: a plain PDF published by the South Dakota Secretary of State (Division of Elections) that reprints the statute text word for word with its 'Source:' lines. The Legislature's own code site (https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/12) serves the helper only a script shell (157 characters of text), so it was not read. The orchestrator should decide whether a Secretary of State reprint counts as the state's own site; it is statute text, not a guide.

ties.applies_to: a tie vote found on the canvass of the original official returns for an office or position, in an election covered by chapter 12-21 (not school, township or municipal elections, which have their own sections) (SDCL 12-21-16 and 12-21-43)
ties.steps: the canvassing board certifies the tied vote to the county auditor (election confined to a county) or to the secretary of state (all other elections); that officer proceeds as if a petition for a recount of all votes involved had been filed, and the recount is made; if a tie is found on the recount and it cannot be determined who is nominated or elected, the authority charged with issuing the certificate fixes a time and place and the candidates draw lots, in person or by representative, and the certificate is issued accordingly
ties.who: the county auditor or the secretary of state (recount); the authority charged by law with issuing the certificate of election or nomination (lot)

sources.quote: Whenever by reason of a tie vote found to exist upon the canvass of the original official returns, it is impossible to declare who has been elected or nominated to an office or position, it shall thereupon be the duty of the official board making such canvass to certify said vote to the county auditor where the election involved is confined to or within the limits of a county, and to the secretary of state as to all other elections.

Thereupon such county auditor or such secretary of state, as the case may be, shall proceed exactly as if a petition had been duly filed under §§ 12-21-7 to 12-21-15, inclusive, requiring a recount to be made of all votes [...] involved, and such recount shall proceed accordingly.

When a tie vote between candidates is found to exist on the basis of any such recount, and by reason of such tie vote it cannot be determined who has been nominated or elected, it shall be the duty of the authority charged by law with the responsibility of issuing the certificate of election or nomination to fix a time and place for the drawing of lots by such candidates involved in such tie vote

ties.note: The text says 'an office or position' and 'nominated or elected' and names no kind of office; the kinds are a mapping [inferred]. Presidential electors are covered by the same words and by the recount in 12-21-15 [inferred]. Whether the South Dakota Constitution gives the Legislature a role for a tie for governor or in judging its members' elections was not read (the Secretary of State's book reprints only some constitutional provisions and none on this was found). Township elections were not read. Under 12-21-18 chapter 12-21 does not apply to an election that must be followed by a runoff for want of a majority.

ties.applies_to: municipal governing-body elections: a tie vote after a canvass of the original official returns (SDCL 9-13-27.2)
ties.steps: the governing body certifies the tied vote to the finance officer, who notifies the candidates that unless a recount is requested in writing within five days the winner is determined by drawing of lots; if no recount is requested, or a tie is found on the recount, the finance officer fixes the time and place and the drawing of lots is held in the manner the finance officer directs, and the certificate goes to the winner

sources.quote: If a tie vote exists after a canvass of original official returns, the governing body making the canvass shall certify the vote to the finance officer. The finance officer shall then notify the candidates that if no request for recount is made in writing to the finance officer within five days after the certification, the winner shall be determined by drawing of lots.

ties.note: A recount is optional here (the candidates may request it); the lot follows whether or not one is made. Municipal charters were not read; state general law only.

ties.applies_to: school board elections: a tie vote after the canvass of the original official returns (SDCL 13-7-19.1)
ties.steps: the school board certifies the tied vote to the business manager, who notifies the candidates that unless a recount is requested in writing within five days the winner is determined by drawing of lots; if no recount is requested, or a tie is found on the recount, the business manager fixes the time and place and the drawing of lots is held in the manner the business manager directs

sources.quote: If a tie vote exists after the canvass of the original official returns, the school board making the canvass shall certify the vote to the business manager. The business manager shall then notify the candidates that if no request for recount is made in writing to the business manager within five days, the winner shall be determined by drawing of lots.

ties.note: School district elections are carved out of 12-21-16 and 12-21-6.

ties.applies_to: a first primary for U.S. Senate, U.S. House or Governor with three or more candidates in which no candidate receives thirty-five percent of the votes of the candidate's party, when there is a tie for second place and no tie for first place (SDCL 12-6-51.1)
ties.steps: all candidates tying for second place are placed along with the first-place candidate on the ballot for a runoff election held eight weeks after the first primary; the person receiving the highest number of votes at the runoff is nominated
ties.who: the voters of the party, at the runoff

sources.quote: If there is a tie for second place in the first primary election and there is no tie for first place, all tying second place candidates must be placed along with the first place candidate on the ballot for the runoff election.

ties.note: A tie for first place in such a primary, or a primary tie in any other race, falls under the first rule above (recount, then lot) [inferred]; the runoff rule itself says nothing about a tie for first place.

ties.steps: no provision found saying what a tie vote on a question does
ties.note: Read: SDCL 12-21 (recounts, all sections 12-21-1 to 12-21-54 headings, 12-21-6 to 12-21-19, 12-21-42, 12-21-43 in full), 12-20-39 and a search of the whole Title 12 reprint for tie, tied, by lot and equal number of votes. The tie sections speak of candidates and of 'an office or position'. An absence cannot be confirmed from a reprint search alone.

threshold.conditions: a tie vote on the canvass of the original official returns that makes it impossible to declare who has been elected or nominated; does not apply to school and township elections
threshold.in_words: a recount of all the votes involved happens when the canvass shows a tie

recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read (the compensation of the two non-referee recount board members is set by the governing body of the jurisdiction, 12-21-4)

sources.quote: Thereupon such county auditor or such secretary of state, as the case may be, shall proceed exactly as if a petition had been duly filed under §§ 12-21-7 to 12-21-15, inclusive, requiring a recount to be made of all votes [...] involved, and such recount shall proceed accordingly. This section shall not apply to school and township elections.

recounts.note: The section's heading is 'Tie vote certified by canvassing board--Automatic recount'. The kinds are a mapping of 'an office or position' [inferred].

threshold.percent_of: the total vote cast for all candidates for such office, position, or nomination (for an office with two or more seats, twice the average votes of those declared elected, 12-21-13)
threshold.conditions: an office, position or nomination voted upon only by the voters of one county or part thereof; verified petition to the county auditor within three days after the official county canvass (nonlegislative) or the official state canvass (legislative), stating the candidate believes a recount will change the result
threshold.in_words: a defeated candidate whose margin does not exceed two percent of the total vote cast for all candidates may ask for a recount

who_may_request: the defeated candidate, by verified petition to the county auditor
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read

sources.quote: A candidate for any office, position, or nomination which is voted upon only by the voters of one county or part thereof may [...] ask for a recount of the official returns if such candidate is defeated, according to the official returns, by a margin not exceeding two percent of the total vote cast for all candidates for such office, position, or nomination.

recounts.note: State legislative districts inside one county come under this section; those spanning counties under 12-21-11 (next). Municipal and school elections have their own sections (below).

threshold.percent_of: the total vote cast for all candidates for the office
threshold.conditions: a legislative district comprising more than one county; petition to the secretary of state within three days after completion of the official canvass by the State Board of Canvassers; the recount must be completed within fourteen days of filing
threshold.in_words: a defeated candidate for the Legislature in a multi-county district whose margin does not exceed two percent of the total vote cast for all candidates may petition for a recount

who_may_request: the defeated candidate for election to or nomination for the Legislature, by petition to the secretary of state
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read

sources.quote: If any legislative district comprises more than one county, any candidate for election to or nomination for the Legislature who, according to the official returns, has been defeated by a margin not exceeding two percent of the total vote cast for all candidates for the office may, within three days after completion of the official canvass by the State Board of Canvassers, file a petition with the secretary of state

threshold.percent_of: the total vote cast for all candidates for the office, position, or nomination
threshold.conditions: an office, position or nomination other than the Legislature voted upon in more than one county; petition to the secretary of state within three days after completion of the official canvass by the State Board of Canvassers
threshold.in_words: a defeated candidate for a multi-county office other than the Legislature whose margin does not exceed one-fourth of one percent of the total vote may petition for a recount

who_may_request: the defeated candidate, by petition to the secretary of state
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read

sources.quote: If any candidate for an office, position, or nomination other than the Legislature is voted upon in more than one county, and has been defeated, according to the official returns, by a margin which does not exceed one-fourth of one percent of the total vote cast for all candidates for the office, position, or nomination, the candidate may, within three days after completion of the official canvass by the State Board of Canvassers, file a petition with the secretary of state

recounts.note: Covers U.S. Senate, U.S. House (at large) and statewide offices by the words 'voted upon in more than one county' [inferred for the kinds]; a county office spanning counties falls here as well.

threshold.percent_of: the total of votes cast for both groups of candidates
threshold.conditions: petition to the secretary of state at any time after the election and before the canvass by the State Board of Canvassers; recount in all precincts in all counties
threshold.in_words: if one group of candidates for presidential electors appears elected over another by a margin not exceeding one-fourth of one percent of the votes cast for both groups, a petition may be filed for a recount of all votes

who_may_request: the chairman of the state central committee of the party that nominated the groups of candidates
any two or more candidates of either group
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read

sources.quote: it fairly appears that one group of candidates for presidential electors has been elected over another group of candidates by a margin not exceeding one-fourth of one percent of the total of votes cast for both groups of candidates, the chairman of the state central committee of the political party that nominated the groups of candidates, or any two or more candidates of either group, may file with the secretary of state

threshold.percent_of: the total vote cast for and against on the question
threshold.conditions: a referred or submitted question voted upon throughout the state; petition to the secretary of state within ten days after the official canvass, signed by not less than 1,000 registered voters representing at least five counties; recount in all precincts of the counties that voted
threshold.in_words: a statewide question decided by a margin not exceeding one-fourth of one percent of the vote for and against may be recounted on a petition of at least 1,000 registered voters from at least five counties

who_may_request: not less than one thousand registered voters of the state, representing at least five counties
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read

sources.quote: Whenever any referred or submitted question is voted upon throughout the state and is determined according to the official canvass by a margin of not exceeding one-fourth of one percent of the total vote cast for and against on such question, there may be filed with the secretary of state within ten days after the completion of the official canvass by the State Board of Canvassers, a petition signed by not less than one thousand registered voters of the state, and representing at least five counties of the state

threshold.conditions: petition within ten days after the election by any three registered voters of a precinct, verified, stating that they believe the official returns from the precinct are erroneous as to a specified candidate or question; a further precinct may be petitioned within three days of the first petition
threshold.in_words: no margin condition: any three registered voters of a precinct may petition within ten days for a recount of that precinct on a candidate or question

who_may_request: any three registered voters of a precinct, by verified petition to the officer in charge of the election
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read

sources.quote: When within ten days after an election any three registered voters of a precinct file with the officer in charge of the election a petition, duly verified by them, setting forth that they believe that the official returns from such precinct as to a specified candidate or as to a specified referred or submitted question are erroneous, the votes of such precinct as to the office or position specified or as to the question specified shall be recounted.

recounts.note: A precinct-by-precinct recount, not a whole-contest recount. Chapter 12-21 does not apply to school and municipal elections (12-21-6) or to an election that must be followed by a runoff (12-21-18).

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for all candidates for the office
threshold.conditions: candidate for the municipal governing body; written request to the municipal finance officer within five days after completion of the official canvass; recount within ten days of the request by a board chosen by the candidates
threshold.in_words: a defeated municipal governing-body candidate whose margin is not over two percent of the votes cast for all candidates, or is five votes or less, may request a recount

who_may_request: the defeated candidate, by written request to the municipal finance officer
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read

sources.quote: If any candidate for the municipal governing body is defeated by a margin not exceeding two percent of the total votes cast for all candidates for the office, or by a margin of five votes or less, the candidate may, within five days after completion of the official canvass, file with the municipal finance officer a written request for a recount.

recounts.note: Municipal ballot questions: a recount is conducted on a petition of three registered voters within five days if the question was decided by a margin not exceeding two percent of the votes cast (SDCL 9-13-27.4, not quoted as a rule).

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for all candidates for the office
threshold.conditions: candidate for the school board; written request to the school district business manager within five days after completion of the official canvass
threshold.in_words: a defeated school board candidate whose margin does not exceed two percent of the votes cast for all candidates may request a recount

who_may_request: the defeated candidate, by written request to the business manager
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read

sources.quote: If any candidate for the school board is defeated by a margin not exceeding two percent of the total votes cast for all candidates for the office, the candidate may, within five days after completion of the official canvass, file with the business manager of the school district a written request for a recount.

unread.what: who pays for a recount; township elections; the South Dakota Constitution's rules on a tie for governor or the Legislature's judging of its members' elections; municipal and school ballot-question recounts beyond the one noted

notes: The Secretary of State's PDF reprints Title 12 with the statutes in effect on July 1, 2026; the same text was not cross-checked against the Legislature's site because that site serves only a script shell.
South Dakota recounts a tie automatically and then, if still tied, draws lots (state and county offices); in municipal and school elections a tie goes to lots after an optional recount.
